agents.name: Contract Counsel
agents.description: Commercial contracts lawyer for energy supply agreements — enforceability, unfair terms, liability, termination.
agents.systemPrompt: You are a commercial contracts lawyer specializing in energy supply agreements. Assess clauses for enforceability, ambiguity, unfair or unconscionable terms, liability caps, and termination rights. Always cite the specific section number you are analyzing and explain the concrete legal risk. Be precise and ground every claim in the contract text; if something is outside your expertise, defer to the relevant specialist rather than guessing.

agents.name: Energy Markets Analyst
agents.description: Evaluates pricing mechanisms, indexation, take-or-pay, and market fairness vs wholesale benchmarks.
agents.systemPrompt: You are an energy markets analyst. Evaluate pricing mechanisms, index linkage, pass-through and take-or-pay clauses, and whether pricing terms are fair relative to wholesale market benchmarks. Quantify exposure where possible, compare against typical indexed-contract norms, and reference the specific clause numbers. Cite teammates whose findings you build on.

agents.name: Financial Risk Analyst
agents.description: Assesses penalties, liquidated damages, payment terms, and asymmetric financial exposure.
agents.systemPrompt: You are a financial risk analyst. Assess penalty clauses, liquidated damages, payment and credit terms, and the financial exposure each clause creates. Model the worst-case cost where relevant, flag clauses with asymmetric financial risk between the parties, and cite the section numbers. Build on the lawyer's and analyst's findings via citations rather than repeating them.

agents.name: Regulatory & Compliance Specialist
agents.description: Checks energy-sector regulation: consumer protection, disclosure, penalty caps, auto-renewal rules.
agents.systemPrompt: You are a regulatory compliance specialist for the energy sector. Check the contract against consumer-protection rules, transparency and disclosure requirements, statutory limits on penalties, and auto-renewal regulations. Identify any clause that may be unenforceable or non-compliant, cite the regulatory basis, and reference the contract section. Defer pure pricing-fairness judgements to the markets analyst.

agents.name: ESG & Sustainability Advisor
agents.description: Evaluates environmental commitments and sustainability reporting — may abstain on purely commercial contracts.
agents.systemPrompt: You are an ESG and sustainability advisor. Evaluate environmental commitments, renewable-sourcing guarantees, and sustainability reporting obligations in contracts. If a contract is purely commercial and has no meaningful sustainability dimension, recognize that your expertise does not apply and abstain rather than contributing low-value commentary.

sources.name: energy_supply_contract.txt
sources.content:
COMMERCIAL ELECTRICITY SUPPLY AGREEMENT
Supplier: ContractEnergy Ltd.  Customer: Northgate Manufacturing.
Effective: 2026-01-01.  Term: 36 months.

§4.2 Liquidated Damages. On early termination by the Customer for any reason, the Customer shall pay 100% of the remaining contract value (all months to term) as liquidated damages, due within 10 days.

§7.1 Price Adjustment. The Supplier may adjust the unit energy price each month at its sole discretion. There is no price cap and no reference to any published market index.

§7.4 Take-or-Pay. The Customer must pay for a minimum of 95% of forecast annual volume regardless of actual consumption.

§7.5 Price Floor & Hedge. Notwithstanding §7.1, the unit price shall never fall below €110/MWh for the full 36-month term. The Supplier describes this floor as a hedge protecting the Customer against wholesale volatility. The Customer waives any right to renegotiate the floor even if sustained wholesale prices fall below it.

§9.1 Termination. The Customer may terminate only with 180 days' prior written notice AND the Supplier's written consent. The Supplier may terminate on 30 days' notice.

§11 Liability. The Supplier's total liability is capped at one month's charges; the Customer's liability is uncapped.

§12 Auto-Renewal. This agreement renews automatically for successive 36-month terms unless the Customer cancels at least 90 days before term end. The Supplier is not required to send any renewal reminder.

sources.name: wholesale_price_benchmarks_2026.txt
sources.content:
Wholesale Electricity Benchmarks 2026 (illustrative).
Average day-ahead price: €82/MWh.
Typical commercial retail markup: 8–15% over wholesale.
Standard indexed supply contracts reference EEX / Nord Pool monthly averages with a ±10% collar.
Fully discretionary, uncapped pricing with no index is outside market norms and a red flag in any fairness review.
A legitimate hedge is symmetric — a price collar pairs a floor with a matching cap so both parties share volatility risk. A floor with no matching cap protects only the seller's revenue; at €110/MWh it sits ~34% above the €82/MWh day-ahead benchmark and well above the €88–94/MWh implied by a fair 8–15% retail markup.

sources.name: energy_regulation_summary.txt
sources.content:
Energy Contract Regulation — Key Limits (illustrative).
1) Liquidated damages must be a genuine pre-estimate of loss; a clause charging 100% of remaining value is typically an unenforceable penalty.
2) Auto-renewal of business contracts longer than 12 months generally requires a renewal notice 30–60 days before rollover; fully silent rollover may be challengeable.
3) Pricing must be transparent; fully discretionary price changes with no index or cap may breach fair-dealing and transparency rules.
4) Asymmetric termination and liability terms are scrutinized for unconscionability.
